messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: Elevated 502/504 rates observed for tenant 'HastingsCo' on private VPC (prod-dedicated). Automatic routing fallback engaged. Paging oncall.

ian (oncall): saw the page. checking console now. how widespread? any region-specific impact?

olivia (solutions): customer reports spike starting ~08:42 UTC. Only their private deployment (vpc-3462) on us-east-1. Observed 502s from app -> NLB -> backend.

ian (oncall): tagging netops. @raj can you check NLB target health for vpc-3462 (target group tg-hastings-prod)?

raj (netops): running describe-target-health...

raj (netops): ```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/tg-hastings-prod/abc123
# output summary
TargetHealthDescriptions:
 - 10.2.3.12: unhealthy (Reason: SecurityGroup) 
 - 10.2.3.13: healthy
 - 10.2.3.14: unhealthy (Connection timed out)
```

dana (sre): interesting, mixed target states. any recent security group changes pushed to the customer VPC?

olivia (solutions): customer says they applied a host-level hardening change yesterday evening, security team updated `hastings-app-sg` to drop ephemeral ports.

ian (oncall): that would break NLB healthchecks if source ports changed. what are our NLB health check source IPs?

raj (netops): NLB health checks come from internal targets. health check path is `/healthz`. Health check type TCP/HTTP on port 8080. I'd like to run a curl from an instance in same subnet: `curl -v http://10.2.3.12:8080/healthz`

olivia (solutions): tom (customer-eng) is on the line with Hastings. Tom, can you run that on a bastion?

tom (customer-eng): running now from bastion (10.2.0.5):
```
curl -v http://10.2.3.12:8080/healthz
* Rebuilt URL to: http://10.2.3.12:8080/healthz
*   Trying 10.2.3.12...
* connect to 10.2.3.12 port 8080 failed: Connection refused
* Failed to connect to 10.2.3.12 port 8080: Connection refused
```

ian (oncall): connection refused on unhealthy target. for healthy one?

tom (customer-eng): 10.2.3.13 returns 200.

dana (sre): pattern: some hosts blocked by SG changes. we should request a quick rollback of the last SG rule or add explicit allow for NLB -> instance ephemeral/healthcheck ports.

raj (netops): also seeing occasional DNS timeouts from the control plane when routing to that tenant's private control plane endpoint — may be unrelated but worth noting.

olivia (solutions): customer security says they won't rollback without approval. could we mitigate from our side? options: 1) switch NLB to use TLS termination and healthchecks on 443 (no, backend still blocked) 2) move affected targets out of rotation (drain) and rely on healthy ones — but they want full capacity. 3) temporary rule to allow internal load balancer healthcheck CIDR.

ian (oncall): we should attempt least-priv change: ask customer to add allow rule for healthcheck from NLB/ELB healthcheck range (or allow 10.2.0.0/16 internal). If they won't, we can failover traffic to their DR pool in us-west-2 (they have dedicated pool there).

tom (customer-eng): security will allow a scoped temporary rule for NLB healthchecks if we provide exact sources. what source IPs do healthchecks come from?

raj (netops): healthchecks originate from the NLB nodes, unpredictable IPs within the subnet. Recommend permitting the NLB security group (sg-nlb-hastings) as a source in the instance SG `hastings-app-sg`. Suggest rule: `Allow TCP 8080 from sg-nlb-hastings` for 30 minutes.

olivia (solutions): tom — can you ask ops to add that rule as an exception? we'll monitor then roll back.

ian (oncall): meanwhile, I'm going to cordon the unhealthy targets to reduce 502 noise so customer app doesn't get routed to bad hosts: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <tg> --targets Id=10.2.3.12`

raj (netops): I'm prepping the drain. execute when customer confirms SG change or we accept increased error exposure.

tom (customer-eng): ops added rule: `Allow TCP 8080 from sg-nlb-hastings`. Confirmed.

ian (oncall): re-check health for 10.2.3.12:
```
curl -v http://10.2.3.12:8080/healthz
* Connected to 10.2.3.12 (10.2.3.12) port 8080
> GET /healthz HTTP/1.1
> Host: 10.2.3.12:8080
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
> Accept: */*
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Content-Type: application/json
< {"ok":true}
```

dana (sre): health now OK. NLB should mark it healthy within the health check interval. I'll pull NLB metrics and keep an eye on 502 rate.

raj (netops): also validated target group: all targets now healthy.

ian (oncall): Routing fallback disabled. Observed 502s dropped to baseline in ~3m.

olivia (solutions): customer confirms application error rate returned to normal. they will schedule a proper SG review and permanent exception for ELB.

ian (oncall): quick runbook notes for postmortem: root cause: host-level SG change removed allow from sg-nlb-hastings -> instance 8080. Mitigation: add SG rule allowing sg-nlb-hastings to instances OR revert host hardening. Short-term: permitted SG rule for 30m. Long-term: update onboarding docs + alerting to detect mixed target health with SG diffs.

ethan (oncall): taking secondary follow-up for 1hr to validate no regressions. leaving channel open.

tom (customer-eng): thanks everyone. customer wants an incident summary and a ticket for permanent firewall exception. I'll open RFC with them.

ian (oncall): creating incident ticket with timeline. assigning postmortem to dana/raj/olivia.

incident-bot: Incident severity downgraded to SEV4 — customer service restored. Please file postmortem within 48h. :white_check_mark:

ian (oncall): closing handoff. if anything flares, re-alert oncall. :phone:
